I'm seeing a similar stack trace using FLAX with 2 x 1080Ti's, I'm using tf.Data to create a pipeline for a FLAX model. I cannot recreated using pure JAX. Also tensorflow and catboost train fine on my GPU's.

I'll try and post more details later - I've uninstalled JAX GPU support for now so I could get some work done.

I have a strong suspicion this issue is fixed at head; we fixed an issue related to accidental sharing of GPU contexts in the same process some months ago. Unfortunately there's not enough detail here for me to reproduce the issue and check.

Closing, on the assumption that this issue is fixed. Please reopen with instructions to reproduce it if you still experience it!

issue.body:
```
$ python3 api_test.py
```

hits the following fatal error on my machine

```
[ RUN      ] APITest.test_issue_1062
2019-09-08 06:14:25.836744: E external/org_tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/xla/python/local_client.cc:731] Execution of replica 1 failed: Invalid argument: executable is built for device CUDA:0 of type "TITAN V"; cannot run it on device CUDA:1 of type "Quadro K2200"
2019-09-08 06:14:30.809031: E external/org_tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/gpu/nccl_all_reduce_thunk.cc:122] This thread has been waiting for 5000ms for and may be stuck: participant for device ordinal 0, stream 0x270b1b0 waiting for all participants to be arrive at rendezvous RendezvousKey{run_id=RunId: 1796, participating_replicas=[0,1], all_reduce_kind=1, op_id=141}
2019-09-08 06:14:35.837040: F external/org_tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/xla/python/local_client.cc:839] Replicated computation launch failed, but not all replicas terminated. Aborting process to work around deadlock. Failure message (there may have been multiple failures, see the error log for all failures): 

executable is built for device CUDA:0 of type "TITAN V"; cannot run it on device CUDA:1 of type "Quadro K2200"
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

Thankfully this is pretty clear about what's going on; it says we compiled for one device but ran on another.  It is also saying we're doing an all-reduce, which is fishy, as XLA does not allow you to target two different GPU models with one XLA computation.  It's possible you're doing this all-reduce between two different XLA computations, but my bet is you're not, in which case...boom.

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 fixes this problem for me.

The test failure isn't that important, but I hit the same problem, this time without a helpful error message, when trying to use trax:

```
python3 -m tensor2tensor.trax.trainer --data_dir=$TMPDIR/trax --dataset=mnist   --model=MLP   --config="train.train_steps=1000"
```

this prints a bunch of

```
2019-09-07 21:38:09.628423: E external/org_tensorflow/tensorflow/stream_executor/stream.cc:332] Error recording event in stream: error recording CUDA event on stream 0x5777730: 
```

and then eventually fails with

```
failed to load in-memory CUBIN: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_SOURCE: device kernel image is invalid
```

full log https://gist.github.com/jlebar/fcb502278cc03019238e677dc6c25896.  Again setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 works around the problem.

I think this is a bug in JAX that it's compiling for one device and then running the computation on another device.  But I'd say it's also a bug somewhere in XLA for not detecting this and printing a nice error in the trax case the way it did in the unit test case.
